gaps.why_now: The existing Phase 9 build step is the smallest honest place to widen runtime pilot coverage from atomic64 and bitmap into the trace-events sample lane.
A trace-events survey gate keeps the Linux sample anchor, starter status, and remaining runtime-substrate blocker explicit while the pilot surface stays small.

A sample-backed lifecycle starter is the first honest runtime-facing trace-events step that can expose the roadmap's shipped selftest hook while modeling bounded event emission and callback registration without pretending full macro or thread parity exists.

A dedicated Phase 9 test file keeps the starter sample reviewable and bounded around the roadmap's lifecycle parity, event emission counts, registration balance, and the stable diagnostics-summary surface.
A narrow differential gate now captures a few foo_bar, template, and function-callback expectations from the Linux sample before any broader runtime substrate work.

A loadable module entry point, runtime task ownership, polling and event-loop substrate, thread creation, and tracepoint registration parity still depend on runtime substrate pieces that the repo has not started yet.
